Seminar Title:

A 10-bit SAR ADC utilizing Chinese Abacus-Unary-Binary CDAC for Implantable Pacemakers.

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Dr. Santanu Sarkar

Speaker Type:

Faculty

Venue:

EC303, Seminar Room.

Date and Time:

09 Nov 2026 3.30PM

Contact:

Dr. Santanu Sarkar

Abstract:

Achieving high linearity and accurate capacitor matching remains a fundamental challenge in capacitive digital to-analog converters (CDACs). In this work, a 10-bit, 833.33 kS/s low-power successive approximation register (SAR) ADC is presented, in which both static and dynamic performance are enhanced through the adoption of a Chinese abacus-unary-binary CDAC architecture. The proposed converter is implemented in a UMC180 nm CMOS process and operates at a supply voltage of 1.8 V. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SAR ADC dissipates approximately 91.57 µW. The converter exhibits excellent static linearity, achieving a differential nonlinearity (DNL) of 1.18 LSB and an integral nonlinearity (INL) of 1.52 LSB. In terms of dynamic performance, the ADC attains a signal to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 61.53 dB, a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 81.43 dB, and an effective number of bits (ENOB) of 9.93 bits for an input frequency of 10.5794 kHz at a sampling rate of 833.33 kS/s. Furthermore, the dynamic performance is also evaluated over a range of input frequencies approaching the Nyquist frequency of 416.66 kHz, confirming the reliability and stability of the converter under varying operating conditions. Finally, a comprehensive power breakdown analysis is presented to quantify the contribution of individual circuit blocks to the overall power consumption.
